title: AI Overviews, AI Mode and ChatGPT Search: What Is the Difference?
h1: AI Overviews, AI Mode and ChatGPT Search: what is the difference?
desc: A plain comparison of three ways people get AI answers, what each means for a business owner, and the work that helps with all of them, without unverified claims.
lead: They are three different experiences with a shared principle: the tool builds an answer and shows sources. For a business, most of the useful work is the same for all three.
body:
Business owners ask me whether they need a different strategy for each. My answer: the experiences differ, but the foundation is the same. I will describe the differences at the level I can stand behind and avoid details I cannot verify.

Google AI Overviews

A summary Google may place above some search results, with links to supporting pages. The user did not choose to start an AI conversation; it appears inside normal search for some queries. Per Google, a page must be indexed and eligible to show a snippet to appear as a supporting link, and no special markup is required. See the AI Overviews entry.

Google AI Mode

A conversational experience in Google where the user asks longer questions and follows up, with links to sources. It has the same eligibility principle as above. See AI Mode in the glossary.

ChatGPT search

ChatGPT can search the web to answer. OpenAI documents separate crawlers: OAI-SearchBot is used for ChatGPT search, GPTBot for training, and ChatGPT-User acts for users. You can control them separately in robots.txt.

What I cannot tell you

How any of them decides what to mention is not public, and answers vary between runs, users and countries. Anyone who claims exact rules is guessing. Test your own questions instead.

What helps with all three

This part is practice from my work:

  1. Be reachable. Do not block the crawlers you want, and make sure key pages are indexed.
  2. Be clear. One definition sentence for your business, used consistently.
  3. Answer first. Begin each section with a direct answer.
  4. Be consistent. The same facts on your site, Maps and profiles.
  5. Measure. Ask real customer questions in each tool and record the results.

At Qoyod, I captured results with real Arabic questions: ChatGPT put it first for "best Saudi websites with free accounting templates", Gemini named it first for the easiest accounting system for VAT, and Google AI Mode listed it first for best cloud accounting software in Saudi Arabia. These are captured results for those specific questions at the time, not guarantees.

Three myths I hear

  • "I need special files for each tool." Google says no special markup is required for its AI features. For OpenAI's crawlers, robots.txt is the documented control.
  • "If I rank first, I will be named." Ranking in the list and being named in a generated answer are different outcomes, and one does not guarantee the other.
  • "The tools all give the same answer." They do not, and the same tool varies between runs. That is why I test more than once.

If you only have time for one habit, make it the monthly test: the same ten questions, on the same tools, written into the same sheet. After three months you will see a trend, and the trend is more useful than any opinion, including mine.

Where to begin

Start with a baseline. Ask your customers' questions on each tool and write down what you see. The free visibility test can prepare the questions. Read the Qoyod case study for the full approach.
faq: Do I need a different strategy for each tool?
The experiences differ, but the foundation is the same: be reachable, clear, consistent and answer first. Then test each tool separately.
Which one matters most for my business?
It depends on where your customers search. Ask a few of them, and test your questions on each tool.
Can I block one and allow another?
For the crawlers OpenAI documents, yes, through robots.txt. Google offers its own controls, which I describe in the robots.txt article.
